newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to place Lufthansa stake this year.
newsitem.headline: Germany to place Lufthansa stake this year.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel will give government finances a year-end filip by selling the state's 35.7 percent stake in national carrier Lufthansa to a development agency, officials said on Friday.

Leaders from Germany's three-party coalition agreed this week to make the transfer -- a prelude to proper privatisation -- after junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) gave up their objections.

But FDP parliamentary party chief Hermann Otto Solms said the transfer could go ahead only if the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) agency acted as a temporary trustee and Lufthansa was sold off completely next year.
"The goal remains a full and rapid privatisation. The state share should be floated to a wide range of buyers by the end of 1997 at the latest," Solms said in a statement.
Solms added that the move would mean that the government incurred no costs. He said documents readying Lufthansa for final privatisation should be completed as soon as possible.
The sale could net 2.9 billion marks ($1.9 billion) for federal coffers strained by a big spending overshoot this year which will take the total budget deficit up to 3.75 percent of GDP.

The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung quoted an official from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) as saying the sale would enable federal borrowing to be held to 73 billion marks this year, up from an originally planned 60 billion.
Germany agreed in November with the European Commission that the terms of the sale could ensure that control of Lufthansa would not fall into foreign hands after privatisation.
If this happened it would mean the airline would lose some of the competitive advantages it enjoys as a national carrier.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.557 German Marks)
